summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, regulation.

articles.title: California takes CoinFlip to task
articles.description: The state ordered the crypto ATM company to pay $4.8 million to scam victims, and bashed federal regulators over failing to police for fraud.

articles.title: Shift4 signals caution
articles.description: The payments processor is navigating weak demand for travel to Europe, and softer sales at its restaurant and hotel customers.

articles.title: NCR Atleos, First Citizens lock arms
articles.description: The bank aims to expand its reach to more customers by offering services via the NCR Atleos ATMs in Target stores.

articles.title: Will a ‘blue wave’ push the CCCA?
articles.description: With Sen. Roger Marshall voted out and Sen. Dick Durbin retiring, the Credit Card Competition Act faces an uncertain future.

articles.title: Cards draw customers, Marqeta CEO says
articles.description: Companies have found there’s “almost nothing more engaging than a card,” CEO Mike Milotich said this week in an interview.

articles.title: FIS, Toast CFOs exit
articles.description: The chief financial officers are leaving the payments players as the companies grapple with separate challenges.

articles.title: Block reaches $964M DOJ pact
articles.description: The company would pay $764 million of the amount in the agreement to resolve U.S. charges that its anti-money laundering program was ineffective.

articles.title: Payments firm settles FTC fees case
articles.description: Riverside Payments and its affiliates agreed to pay $600,000 to resolve allegations they misled small businesses about processing costs.
